title: Cut a twisted paper loop in half: you get one ring
pause_note: v5, Why Is It Designed Like That? / Everyday Physics, hook=try len=short look=flat. DO hook at 0 s: a big yellow paper loop with ONE half twist (Mobius strip) on a green cutting mat, scissors already moving along the inked centre line, title 'Cut it in half.' (frame 0 never shows the result). Wrong guess (two rings) shown as two ghost rings and struck out at ~5 s on 'Nope'. Strongest event at ~7.8 s on 'one': the cut closes and the paper springs open into ONE ring twice as long. Why explained inside the strip: a gold paint stroke runs along one half, the twist hands it to the other half, it needs two laps to get home. Consequence: a 1/3 cut gives two rings, linked (shown). One-word ending 'Two?' echoes the wrong guess; the linked pair folds back into the frame-0 loop. No mascot. Avoid saying 'Mobius' (ASR); it is on screen as a label only.

beats: Half-twist a paper loop and cut it down the middle.
It falls open into one long ring.
Follow one half. The twist joins it to the other half.
So both halves are one strip, twice as long.
Cut a third from the edge instead: two rings, linked.
